# Nango on this machine, for the harness's `nango` tool (SETUP.md, "Connected accounts").
# The free self-hosted edition is Nango's auth + proxy, which is all the tool uses.
#
#   cp .env.example .env      # then put a key in it: openssl rand -base64 32
#   docker compose up -d      # dashboard: http://localhost:3003
#
# Adapted from github.com/NangoHQ/nango/blob/master/docker-compose.yaml:
# - every port is bound to 127.0.0.1. The stock file publishes Postgres (password "nango"), Redis
#   and the API on all interfaces, so anyone on the network could reach them; here the secret key
#   only works from this machine.
# - no providers.yaml mount (it needs a checkout of the Nango repo; the image has its own copy)
# - the database lives in a named volume (a Windows folder bind mount trips up Postgres permissions)
name: jev-nango

services:
  nango-db:
    image: postgres:16.0-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: nango
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: nango
      POSTGRES_DB: nango
    volumes:
      - nango-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    restart: unless-stopped

  nango-redis:
    image: redis:7.2.4
    restart: unless-stopped

  nango-server:
    # "hosted" follows Nango's latest release; pin a tag from hub.docker.com/r/nangohq/nango-server/tags
    # if an update ever breaks something
    image: nangohq/nango-server:hosted
    platform: linux/amd64        # Apple silicon: runs under Rosetta (Docker Desktop > Settings > General)
    environment:
      NANGO_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${NANGO_ENCRYPTION_KEY:?put a key in nango/.env (openssl rand -base64 32)}
      NANGO_DB_HOST: nango-db
      NANGO_DB_USER: nango
      NANGO_DB_PASSWORD: nango
      NANGO_DB_NAME: nango
      RECORDS_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://nango:nango@nango-db:5432/nango
      SERVER_PORT: 3003
      NANGO_SERVER_URL: http://localhost:3003          # OAuth redirect: http://localhost:3003/oauth/callback
      NANGO_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL: http://localhost:3000   # (the stock default)
      FLAG_SERVE_CONNECT_UI: "true"                    # the page connect links open, on :3009
      CSP_REPORT_ONLY: "true"
      NANGO_LOGS_ENABLED: "false"
      LOG_LEVEL: info
      # dashboard login (nango/.env): FLAG_AUTH_ENABLED=false drops Nango's accounts; then an optional
      # NANGO_DASHBOARD_USERNAME/PASSWORD pair puts the dashboard behind a browser password prompt
      FLAG_AUTH_ENABLED: ${FLAG_AUTH_ENABLED:-true}
      NANGO_DASHBOARD_USERNAME: ${NANGO_DASHBOARD_USERNAME:-}
      NANGO_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD: ${NANGO_DASHBOARD_PASSWORD:-}
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:3003:3003"
      - "127.0.0.1:3009:3009"
    depends_on:
      - nango-db
    restart: unless-stopped

name: jev-nango

services:
  nango-db:
    image: postgres:16.0-alpine
    environment:
      POSTGRES_USER: nango
      POSTGRES_PASSWORD: nango
      POSTGRES_DB: nango
    volumes:
      - nango-data:/var/lib/postgresql/data
    restart: unless-stopped

  nango-redis:
    image: redis:7.2.4
    restart: unless-stopped

  nango-server:
    # "hosted" follows Nango's latest release; pin a tag from hub.docker.com/r/nangohq/nango-server/tags
    # if an update ever breaks something
    image: nangohq/nango-server:hosted
    platform: linux/amd64        # Apple silicon: runs under Rosetta (Docker Desktop > Settings > General)
    environment:
      NANGO_ENCRYPTION_KEY: ${NANGO_ENCRYPTION_KEY:?put a key in nango/.env (openssl rand -base64 32)}
      NANGO_DB_HOST: nango-db
      NANGO_DB_USER: nango
      NANGO_DB_PASSWORD: nango
      NANGO_DB_NAME: nango
      RECORDS_DATABASE_URL: postgresql://nango:nango@nango-db:5432/nango
      SERVER_PORT: 3003
      NANGO_SERVER_URL: http://localhost:3003          # OAuth redirect: http://localhost:3003/oauth/callback
      NANGO_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL: http://localhost:3000   # (the stock default)

Train on non-consecutive days (e.g., Mon / Wed / Fri). For each exercise, pick a weight you can finish with **2–3 reps in reserve (RPE 7–8)** — the last rep should feel hard but keep your form clean; leaving reps in the bank is what lets you recover and get stronger without wrecking your joints.

**Warm-up (10 min):** 5 min easy cardio (brisk walk or bike) + 2 light ramp-up sets of goblet squats at half your working weight (~10 reps each).

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|

| Dumbbell row (each side) | 4 × 10 | 60 s |
| Plank | 3 × 20–30 s | 60 s |

**Cardio:** 10 min easy cycling or brisk walk, at a conversational pace (RPE 4–5).

## Day 2 — Hinge Focus

**Warm-up (10 min):** 5 min easy cardio + 2 light ramp-up sets of Romanian deadlifts at half your working weight.

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Dumbbell Romanian deadlift | 4 × 8–10 | 90 s |
| Dumbbell overhead press | 3 × 8–10 | 60–90 s |
| Incline push-ups | 3 × 8–12 | 60 s |
| Glute bridge | 3 × 12–15 | 60 s |

**Cardio:** 10 min easy cycling or brisk walk, at a conversational pace (RPE 4–5).

## Day 3 — Full-Body Mix

**Warm-up (10 min):** 5 min easy cardio + 2 light ramp-up sets of lunges at bodyweight.

| Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Walking lunge (each leg) | 3 × 10 | 60–90 s |
| Dumbbell bench press | 3 × 8–10 | 60–90 s |
| Wide-grip dumbbell row (each side) | 4 × 10–12 | 60 s |
| Side plank (each side) | 2 × 20–30 s | 45 s |

**Cardio:** 10–15 min easy cycling or brisk walk, at a conversational pace (RPE 4–5).

## Notes

- **Progression (double progression):** work within each rep range. Once you can hit the top of the range on every set with 2–3 reps left in reserve, add the smallest available increment (~1–2.5 kg / 2.5–5 lb) and restart at the bottom of the range. After 4–6 weeks of steady progress, add one set to the main lift of each day to keep building volume.

- **Safety:** normal muscle soreness is fine; sharp or joint pain is not — stop the exercise and have a professional (physio or doctor) take a look.

# 3-Day Beginner Full-Body Workout

**Intro:** A no-equipment full-body routine for 3 days per week (e.g., Mon/Wed/Fri), with a rest day between sessions; each session takes about 35 minutes.

**Warm-up (each day):** 5 minutes easy walking, then one light set of your first exercise.
**Form & safety:** Move with control, keep a neutral spine, and if you feel sharp or joint pain, stop and check with a professional.
**Progressive overload:** When all sets reach the top of the rep range, add one rep (or a harder variation) at the next session.

## Day 1 — Legs + Push
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Squat (goblet with a dumbbell if at the gym) | 3 x 10–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Push-up (knees OK) | 3 x 8–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Glute bridge | 3 x 12–15 | 60 sec |
| Bent-over row (heavy backpack or dumbbell) | 3 x 10–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Plank | 3 x 20–30 sec | 60 sec |
| **Cardio:** brisk walk | 15 min | — |

## Day 2 — Hinge + Push
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Alternating lunge | 3 x 10 per leg | 60–90 sec |
| Incline push-up (or pike push-up) | 3 x 8–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Romanian deadlift (dumbbell; bodyweight hinge if not) | 3 x 10–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Superman | 3 x 12–15 | 60 sec |
| Bird dog | 3 x 10 per side | 60 sec |
| **Cardio:** brisk walk or easy jog | 15–20 min | — |

## Day 3 — Full-Body Mix
| Exercise | Sets x Reps | Rest |
|---|---|---|
| Step-up (chair or box) | 3 x 10 per leg | 60–90 sec |
| Push-up | 3 x 8–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Row (backpack or dumbbell) | 3 x 10–12 | 60–90 sec |
| Glute bridge march | 3 x 12 per side | 60 sec |
| Plank | 3 x 20–30 sec | 60 sec |
| **Cardio:** brisk walk, or 30 sec jog / 30 sec walk intervals | 20 min | — |

Classic fluffy pancakes — about 12–16 pancakes, 3–4 per person.
**Total time: ~25 minutes** (5 min prep, 15–20 min cooking)

| Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|
| All-purpose flour | 2 cups (240 g) |
| Granulated sugar | 2 tbsp (25 g) |
| Baking powder | 2 tsp |
| Baking soda | ½ tsp |
| Salt | ½ tsp |
| Buttermilk | 2 cups (480 ml) |
| Large eggs | 2 |
| Melted butter | 3 tbsp (40 g) + extra for the pan |
| Maple syrup | to serve |

## Method
1. **Dry mix:** In a large bowl, whisk together the flour, sugar, baking powder, baking soda, and salt.
2. **Wet mix:** In a second bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, and melted butter until smooth.
3. **Combine:** Pour the wet into the dry and stir until *just* combined — lumps are fine, don't overmix. Let the batter rest **5 minutes**.
4. **Heat:** Warm a non-stick pan or griddle over medium heat; lightly butter it.
5. **Cook:** Ladle ¼ cup (60 ml) of batter per pancake. Cook **2–3 minutes** until bubbles form on the surface and the edges look set.
6. **Flip:** Turn and cook **1–2 minutes** more, until golden brown.
7. **Keep warm:** Stack finished pancakes in the oven at 200°F (90°C) while you cook the rest.

## Tips
- If you don't have buttermilk: stir 1 tbsp lemon juice or vinegar into 2 cups of regular milk and let it sit 5 minutes.

- Serve warm with butter and maple syrup.

recipe = """# Fluffy Pancakes (serves 4)

## Ingredients
- 200 g (1¾ cups) plain (all-purpose) flour
- 2 tsp baking powder
- 1 pinch of salt
- 50 g (2 tbsp) sugar
- 300 ml (1¼ cups) milk
- 1 large egg
- 40 g (3 tbsp) butter, melted
- 1 tbsp butter or oil for the pan

## Method
1. Whisk the dry ingredients (flour, baking powder, salt, sugar) in a bowl.
2. Make a well, add the milk, egg and melted butter, and stir until just combined — a few lumps are fine.
3. Rest the batter 5–10 minutes.
4. Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat with a little butter or oil.
5. Pour about ¼ cup (60 ml) of batter per pancake (12–14 pancakes total).
6. Cook 2–3 minutes until bubbles appear on top, flip, and cook 1–2 minutes more until golden.
7. Keep warm in a low oven (100°C / 210°F) while you finish the batch.

## Times
- Prep: 10 minutes
- Cooking: 15–20 minutes
- Total: about 25–30 minutes

## Serves
4 people (about 3–4 pancakes each)

**Tip:** Serve with maple syrup, fresh berries, or a little cream.
"""

plan = """# 3-Day Beginner Full-Body Plan

Three full-body sessions on **non-consecutive days** (e.g., Monday / Wednesday / Friday). Each session: short warm-up → strength → easy cardio. Pick light weights — you should finish every set feeling you could do 2–3 more reps. That's the right effort right now; it keeps you recovering and building the habit.

## Day 1 — Squat & Push
*Why: squat + push + row covers your whole body; the hardest moves come first while you're fresh.*

**Warm-up (5–6 min):** 5 min brisk walk, then 10 easy bodyweight squats and 10 arm circles.

| # | Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest Between Sets |
|---|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Goblet squat (one dumbbell held at chest) | 3 × 10 | 90 sec |
| 2 | Push-up (knees or incline is fine) | 3 × 8–12 | 90 sec |
| 3 | Dumbbell row (one arm, other hand on a bench) | 3 × 10 each side | 60 sec |
| 4 | Seated dumbbell shoulder press | 3 × 10 | 60 sec |
| 5 | Plank | 3 × 20–30 sec | 60 sec |

**Cardio:** 10 min brisk walk — a pace where you can talk in short sentences.

## Day 2 — Hinge & Pull
*Why: the deadlift pattern trains the back and hamstrings — the biggest muscles, and the ones most beginners skip.*

**Warm-up (5–6 min):** 5 min brisk walk, then 10 hip circles and 10 glute bridges.

| # | Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest Between Sets |
|---|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Dumbbell Romanian deadlift | 3 × 10 | 90 sec |
| 2 | Incline push-up (hands on a bench) | 3 × 8–12 | 90 sec |
| 3 | Dumbbell row (one arm, other hand on a bench) | 3 × 10 each side | 60 sec |
| 4 | Glute bridge | 3 × 12 | 60 sec |
| 5 | Dead bug | 3 × 10 each side | 45 sec |

**Cardio:** 10–12 min easy jog (or brisk walk) — conversational pace.

## Day 3 — Legs & Core
*Why: a second squat day plus step-ups builds leg strength safely; side plank adds core stability without any equipment.*

**Warm-up (5–6 min):** 5 min brisk walk, then 10 easy bodyweight squats and 10 arm circles.

| # | Exercise | Sets × Reps | Rest Between Sets |
|---|----------|-------------|-------------------|
| 1 | Goblet squat | 3 × 10 | 90 sec |
| 2 | Step-up onto a low box or sturdy step | 3 × 10 each leg | 60 sec |
| 3 | Push-up (knees or incline is fine) | 3 × 8–12 | 90 sec |
| 4 | Dumbbell row (one arm, other hand on a bench) | 3 × 10 each side | 60 sec |
| 5 | Side plank (on knees is fine) | 3 × 15–20 sec each side | 45 sec |

Makes about 16–20 pancakes (4–5 per person).

## Ingredients

| Ingredient | Amount |
|---|---|
| All-purpose flour | 200 g (1¾ cups) |

|---|---|

| Batter rest | 5 min |

Great pick — 1" is the sweet spot for a reverse sear. Here's the specific plan for the ribeye (assuming it thaws overnight in the fridge, same as the others):

**Before you cook**
- **Dry the surface** — paper towels on all sides, then 15–30 min on a rack. Dry surface = the crust.
- **Salt timing:** if you salted before freezing, you're set. If not, salt generously 45+ min before cooking (not 5 min — that draws out surface moisture and kills the crust).

**The reverse sear (oven → pan)**
1. **Oven: 250°F (121°C)**, steak on a wire rack, until internal hits **125°F (52°C) for medium-rare** — pull ~5°F below the 130°F final; **128°F (53°C) for medium**, pull ~7°F below the 135°F final. For 1", expect **~15–25 min** — this is where an instant-read thermometer earns its keep, because guessing at 1" is where people overshoot.
2. **Sear:** cast iron on high until it just starts to smoke. Thin layer of high-smoke-point oil. **45–60 seconds per side**, plus a 30-second kiss on each long edge if the fat cap is thick. Don't move it mid-sear — that's how the crust forms.
3. **Baste (last 30–45 sec):** a knob of butter, smashed garlic, and thyme, tilting the pan and spooning it over. The butter should sizzle, not foam black.
4. **Rest 5 min**, tented loosely. The ribeye's marbling keeps it forgiving — resting lets the juices redistribute into the center.

**Why this order:** the low oven brings the whole thickness to nearly done *gently*, so the pan's only job is flavor and crust — no fighting a raw middle. That's what makes it easier than a straight sear.

**Watch-outs for ribeye specifically**
- The fat cap renders a lot — keep the pan tilted and drain if it gets rowdy, and watch the fat-cap side so it doesn't char.
- Ribeyes read a little hotter than filets for the same doneness (fat conducts heat), so trust the thermometer over "minutes."
- If the pan isn't smoking yet, wait — searing into a lukewarm pan is the classic way to get steamed, not seared, steak.

Here's one from the early Republic, around 509 BC, when the Etruscan king Lars Porsenna had Rome cornered.

A young Roman named Mucius snuck into Porsenna's camp at night with a sword and a plan: kill the king, and maybe end the siege. He made his way into the tent — where he found not the king alone, but a council of Etruscan nobles. His cover was blown, his sword useless, and the guards took him.

Rather than beg for his life, Mucius did something that stunned the room. He told the king he had no fear of death, and to prove it, he thrust his right hand into the brazier's burning coals and held it there, unmoving, until it was a charred ruin.

Porsenna, shaken, asked if he had anything more to say. Mucius answered only: "Rome sends many men like me."

The king, humbled, released him and sent a letter to Rome offering to end the siege — a truce. Mucius came home a hero, and the Romans gave him a new name: Scaevola, "the left-handed one," because of that burned right hand.

A bit of legend, sure — but it's the kind of story Romans told themselves for centuries: that the city was built on stubbornness.
